name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It regenerates detail in a way that preserves structure—critical for excavation scenes where texture and depth matter more than pure resolution. The trade-off is compute cost: depth-aware upscaling runs slower than standard upscaling, but the quality gain justifies the slowdown for EXCAVA’s high-stakes outputs.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop because it targets resolution, not facial detail—EXCAVA’s core failure is in preserving identity, not texture. The real risk is wasting compute on a tool that doesn’t address the bottleneck. Test it: run InstantX’s upscaler on a face-heavy sample and measure if identity retention improves—if not, drop it and try RealVisXL’s face-focused upscaler instead.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add RealVisXL v1.1’s face model to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. Faces are EXCAVA’s weakest link—every excavation scene with people loses identity, and that breaks immersion faster than any texture flaw. RealVisXL’s face model is purpose-built for photoreal identity retention, so it directly attacks the bottleneck. The trade-off is latency: face-specific models add 15-20% render time per frame, but that’s cheaper than reruns from failed face fidelity.

name: Torque
text: RealVisXL’s face model risks overfitting to its synthetic training set—EXCAVA’s 3D-scanned faces need real-world lighting fidelity, not stylized uniformity. Test it: run RealVisXL on a face-heavy excavation scene with mixed lighting; if identity degrades under harsh shadows, it’s the wrong tool. Better alternative: pair InstantX’s depth-aware upscaler with a face-specific LoRA trained on real excavation footage to preserve identity without synthetic bias.

name: Dynamo
text:
DECISION: Replace RealVisXL v1.1’s face model with **CodeFormer** in EXCAVA’s pipeline to cut identity loss under mixed lighting.

Result must deliver: A side-by-side test showing CodeFormer’s face fidelity vs. RealVisXL on 3D-scanned excavation faces under harsh shadows, with identity retention metrics and compute cost logged. Owner: Torque.
